report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one docstring the diff added states an untrue claim)

The PR is not ready to merge, because the `_trim_unanswered_tool_use` docstring says the method lookup is guarded, and the code does not guard it.
Rule applied: self-contradicting-diff carve-out → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor

1. In `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 278-279, the `_trim_unanswered_tool_use` docstring says the function "Never raises `Exception`" and that "the read, the scan of the stored messages, the method lookup and the call are each guarded and logged at ERROR". The lookup `getattr(store, "truncate_messages", None)` at line 311 runs outside any `try`, and the default only absorbs `AttributeError`. A store whose `truncate_messages` is a property that raises another exception would escape the trim and replace the call's own result. The line `removed = len(conversation.messages) - cut` is also outside a `try`. Either guard the lookup or narrow the docstring. (raised by 1/4 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: the finding disputes the exception net of the trim helper's guards, a functional-coverage gap -->

- VC-4: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — _trim_unanswered_tool_use docstring asserts it never raises Exception because the read, the scan, the method lookup and the call are each guarded and logged at ERROR. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:278]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Read query_database.py:266-361 at head. Guarded by try/except Exception: get_conversation (285-294), the scan _first_unanswered_tool_use (298-307), and the truncate call (322-345). Unguarded: agent.conversation_store (283), len(conversation.messages) (310, after the scan already iterated it), getattr(store, 'truncate_messages', None) (311, which only absorbs AttributeError, so a property raising another exception would propagate, contrary to the docstring's 'method lookup ... guarded'), user.id (323, inside the try, so guarded), and bool(removed_any) (346, unguarded). The rejection line (truncate_messages -> bool, no None) is covered: conversation_store.py declares the bool return, so a falsy value is logged, but it does not address a raising __bool__ or property. A concrete counterexample is a custom store whose truncate_messages property raises RuntimeError. That needs a non-shipped store implementation, so I could not show a shipped caller or documented state producing it. The docstring wording is slightly over-broad but I could not settle FAIL.

  </details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that is cancelled after the agent saved an assistant `tool_use` and before it saved the matching `tool_result` leaves C with exactly the messages it had before that call, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result.
- [ ] With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that ends without cancellation while a `tool_use` it saved has no `tool_result` leaves C cut back to just before the earliest assistant message that call saved with an unanswered `tool_use` — every message before it stays, the call's user message included — logs a WARNING naming C and the number of messages removed, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result. A `tool_use` counts as unanswered when its id, taken from the assistant message's `tool_calls` or from a `tool_use` block in its `provider_content`, has no `role="tool"` message directly after that assistant message.
- [ ] A call that ends without cancellation and saved an unanswered `tool_use` still returns the error it returns today: an `AgentRunError` with the `SQL execution error: ` prefix when the agent returned an error answer, and the same `RuntimeError`, with the same message, that it raises today when `send_message` raised.
- [ ] A call that ends without cancellation and saved no unanswered `tool_use` leaves C's history exactly as the call appended it: a failed call's user message stays ahead of the next call's, as `tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py` pins.
- [ ] When a trim is needed and the conversation store has no `truncate_messages`, or reading the conversation or calling `truncate_messages` raises, the call logs at ERROR naming the store class, leaves the history as it was, and returns or raises the same result it would have without the trim.
- [ ] The change leaves the vendored Anthropic request builder (`_build_payload` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py`) unchanged, so a conversation that reaches it with an unmatched `tool_use` by a path other than `query_database` is still sent as it is.
